# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.

## Objective
- Build a playable 2D top-down Napoleonic Wars strategy game with realistic animations and ragdoll physics in the existing empty PlayGround repo.

## Requirements
- User request: “Make a 2D Napoleonic wars strategy game, with realistic animations, and ragdoll physics, and top down”.
- Browser-based game, responsive and touch-capable; verify visually in a real browser.

## Decisions
- Built a static HTML/CSS/ES-module Canvas 2D game titled **Iron & Eagles — Waterloo, 1815**, no build dependencies.
- Chose real-time tactical combat: select French regiments, right-click/drag move orders, attack orders, formations, hold fire, bayonet charges, morale/rout, artillery, cavalry, objective capture at La Haye Sainte.
- Soldiers are now rendered from pre-generated rotated sprite sheets for performance, while keeping vector detail and 8-frame march + aim/fire/reload/melee poses.
- Ragdolls use Verlet particle constraints with ballistic height (`z`), blood and persistent corpses.
- HUD is HTML over canvas with parchment/brass styling, unit cards, selection panel, minimap, objective tracker, pause/speed, and help.
- Removed full-screen blend modes/backdrop filters to try to improve software-renderer FPS; added mobile pinch-zoom/reworked touch handling.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/utils.js`, `js/terrain.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/ragdoll.js`, `js/units.js`, `js/main.js`.
- Procedural terrain with fields, roads, hedgerows, orchard, farm buildings, pond, trees, crops, flowers, static shadows.
- 13 units (6 French, 7 British), sprites, formation movement, volley fire, artillery projectiles/explosions, cavalry, melee, morale, routing, capture objective, victory/defeat checks.
- HUD, roster cards, minimap, pause, speed, sound, result overlay, desktop/mobile pointer handling, pinch zoom.
- Browser launch and screenshots work after installing Playwright Chromium renderer.
- Verified battle simulation generates combat, smoke, corpses, routs and objective capture.
- Fixed major bugs: missing `Unit.alive` getter (targets never moved/fired), wrong `game.effects.tracers` reference, attack orders being cleared by auto-target scan.

### Active
- Visual/polish pass after latest tweaks (smoke persistence, objective marker, selection range rings, CSS/readability, balance validation).
- Need verify current battle balance after lowering hit chances / adjusting rout and victory conditions.
- Need confirm all game modes/interactions, mobile HUD, pause/result overlays, and animation states via screenshots.

### Blocked
- None functionally. Browser FPS under Playwright SwiftShader/Xvfb is low (~6 FPS) despite ~15 ms JS render time; this is environment/software compositing, not proven game-breaking.
- Latest screenshot command was run after hiding `.grade`; page currently has `.grade` hidden and may have advanced game state. Reload before final verification.

## Next Move
1. Tune/validate combat: run a scripted player advance toward the farm and confirm a reasonable win/loss timeline; ensure objective hold timer and victory conditions feel fair.
2. Strengthen lingering musket smoke, selection firing-range/facing indicators, and objective marker visibility.
3. Fix minor text/UX issues (e.g. “Voltigeurs is taken in flank” grammar; disable/soften action buttons for routing units).
4. Re-check responsive screenshots at desktop and mobile sizes; verify pinch/drag/tap controls.
5. Run final browser test for console errors, victory overlay, replay/observe buttons, and capture polished screenshots.
6. Update README with title, controls, and how to run.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: game shell, HUD markup, loading/result overlays.
- `css/style.css`: full HUD/responsive styling; full-screen `.grade` overlay and hidden `.grain`; recent blend/backdrop removals.
- `js/main.js`: Game class, rendering, camera, input, AI, HUD, objectives, effects, results.
- `js/units.js`: Soldier/Unit classes, sprites, formations, firing, morale, cavalry/artillery, army setup.
- `js/ragdoll.js`: Verlet ragdoll physics and corpse rendering.
- `js/terrain.js`: procedural battlefield map, farm/roads/trees, `WORLD` and `farmZone`.
- `js/audio.js`: WebAudio ambient/musket/cannon/drum/bugle.
- `js/utils.js`: math/noise/geometry/color helpers.
- `screenshots/`: verification captures (`initial.png`, `sprites.png`, `zoom.png`, `battle1.png`, `ui2.png`, `ui3.png`, `nograde.png`).
- `/home/runner/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/output/console-2026-10-31T13-48-29-254Z.log`: browser console errors; currently only favicon 404 after fixes.

## Important Context
- Dev server run in background with `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`; URL `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright CLI browser must be opened with `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`; Chromium was installed with `playwright-cli install-browser chromium`.
- Current test page `.grade` overlay was hidden via eval and game time may have advanced; reload resets the battle.
- Game works without clicking: British AI starts moving at ~16–19s, full advance after 35s; player can pause with Space.
- Balance changes already applied: line/light/guard hit rates `.034/.039/.047`; rout threshold 22; victory if British morale <10, or capture held with morale conditions, or 30s hold; defeat if French morale <4.
- `Unit.alive` getter is essential; don’t regress it.
- Current script likely has a minor typo in `Unit.takeCasualty` message and some unused variables, but no syntax errors (`node --check` passed at last check before latest edits).
- Changes are uncommitted; no git commit or push has been made.

# Iron & Eagles — Waterloo, 1815

A playable, top-down 2D Napoleonic Wars strategy game. Take command of the French **Armée du Nord** at Waterloo: manoeuvre line infantry, light troops, artillery, cuirassiers and the Old Guard, break the Allied line, and take the crossroads at **La Haye Sainte**.

Built with plain HTML, CSS and ES modules on a Canvas 2D renderer. No build step or dependencies.

## Play

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

Or serve the folder with any static web server (the game uses ES modules, so opening `index.html` directly from `file://` will not work).

## Command

| Action | Desktop | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select a regiment | Left click a unit or card, drag a box for several | Tap a unit or card |
| March | Right click the field | Select, then tap the field |
| Attack | Right click an enemy regiment | Select, then tap an enemy |
| Set facing | Right-drag from a unit | — |
| Pan / zoom | WASD or middle-drag / mouse wheel | One-finger drag / pinch |
| Form line or column | `F` or the panel button | Panel button |
| Hold fire | `H` | Panel button |
| Bayonet charge | `C` | Panel button |
| Pause / game speed | `Space` / buttons in the top bar | Pause button |
| Select regiments 1–6 | `1`–`6` | Roster cards |
| Centre on the crossroads | `M` | — |

## Features

- **Real-time tactical combat** with formation movement, volley fire, reload cycles, artillery bombardment, cavalry charges, melee and morale routs.
- **Animated soldiers** drawn from pre-rendered sprite sheets: march, aim, fire, reload and melee poses for French and Allied troops.
- **Ragdoll physics** for casualties, with persistent corpses, blood decals and drifting musket smoke.
- **Objective play**: clear the farm, take La Haye Sainte, then hold the crossroads while the Allied centre breaks.
- **Responsive HUD** with unit cards, selection panel, army morale, minimap, field orders, pause, speed and help.
- **Procedural battlefield**: fields, orchards, hedgerows, roads, the farm and its garden, trees and ambient audio.

## Structure

```
index.html          shell, HUD markup, overlays
css/style.css       HUD, parchment/brass styling and responsive layout
js/main.js          game loop, camera, input, AI, objectives, effects, HUD
js/units.js         soldiers, regiments, sprites, formations, combat
js/ragdoll.js       Verlet ragdoll physics and corpse rendering
js/terrain.js       procedural map and farm objective zone
js/audio.js         WebAudio ambient, muskets, cannon, drums and bugles
js/utils.js         math, noise, geometry and colour helpers
```

## Tips

- Concentrate several regiments on one battalion at a time; spread attacks let the Allies volley each regiment in turn.
- Keep the battery behind the line and let it work the farm before you close.
- Infantry dress at volley range. A **Bayonets** charge closes the distance quickly, but a broken formation will not survive the melee.
- Watch morale, not just numbers. Flanked regiments and battered battalions break early; once a regiment routs it cannot be controlled again.

Help works. The help text is desktop-specific on mobile ("Left click", "right click") but okay; could add touch controls. Maybe update help to mention touch: - "Tap select · drag to pan · pinch to zoom" - "Tap field to march / enemy to attack" Add lines. Good for mobile usability. Let's update the help pop: ```

Tap select · drag to pan · pinch to zoom

Tap field march · tap enemy attack

``` But the help has 7 lines already; adding two makes it taller. It fits at 240 wide and bottom. Maybe combine: - Replace "Left click select · drag for several" with "Click/tap select · drag for several" and "Right click march / attack" with "Right click / tap field to march". Hmm. Let's update: ```

Click / tap select · drag for several

Right click / tap march or attack

Right drag march and dress the line

WASD pan · Wheel zoom · Pinch on touch

... ``` Good. Do that.
